what_it_does: Mamba2 is a newer sequence-processing model that uses state-space equations to represent state instead of the attention mechanism used by traditional transformers. While theoretically efficient, Mamba2 is memory-bound in practice—the amount of time spent waiting for data from memory exceeds the time spent computing—especially because it performs irregular broadcast multiplications and structured sparse (skipped) computations. Neither CPUs nor standard GPUs achieve good efficiency on these operations. This paper presents MambaOPU, an FPGA overlay processor (a programmable layer on top of FPGA hardware) that combines multiple key optimizations: fusing broadcast multiplication with other operations into single hardware instructions, leveraging the sparse structure to skip unnecessary compute, and using a reconfigurable systolic array (a grid of processing units optimized for linear algebra) to improve data reuse.
